style.vernacular: High Andean capital at about 2,800 m in a long valley under Pichincha: a UNESCO colonial old town of whitewashed two- and three-storey houses with clay-tile roofs, wooden balconies, stone portals and central patios around plazas, surrounded by modern concrete, brick and glass districts. Red-brick and rendered mid-rise apartment blocks climb the hillsides; grey andesite stone is used for churches and plazas; eucalyptus, cypress and palms line parks.
style.ornament: Quito School baroque: gold-leaf cedar interiors, carved grey andesite portals and twin domes with green glazed tiles; neoclassical Ionic colonnades and pedimented end pavilions on civic palaces; arcaded portales facing plazas; carved wooden balconies and courtyard fountains; Guayasamin-style monumental modern sculpture.
